clue.text: Gets new actors and delivers more alluring lines?

definitions.meaning: to give the parts in a play to a fresh set of performers
an angler throws out a baited, lure-tipped fishing line again

explanation.surface: A theatre producer changes the cast and hands out more seductive dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: 'alluring' hides a lure, so the lines are fishing lines, thrown out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-assigning roles to fresh performers is the theatrical sense; throwing a fishing line out once more is the angling sense.

clue.text: Stand to project a speech or having done a turn, play guitar?

indicators.note: having turned round, so the little word or is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: A performer either gives a speech or spins round and strums a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link between options but is the letters turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform or podium from which a speaker addresses an audience.

clue.text: Obscure bird seen over dock — pie in the sky?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: to cloud something is to obscure it
the cuckoo is a bird
a ship docks or lands when it comes in to shore

explanation.surface: A mysterious bird glimpsed above a harbour seems a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen over' places the first pieces above the last in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe an unrealistic, idealised fantasy world or hope.

clue.text: Rising Democrat's rep used to bring in A-list celeb

indicators.note: Rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue words bring in, or contain, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rising political figure's representative is deployed to attract a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'to bring in' in the definition; it is the containment signal, leaving 'A-list celeb' as the definition. In a down entry 'Rising' reads the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-tier celebrity of great fame is called a star of the highest order.

clue.text: Serenades perhaps, and kisses with no upset

indicators.note: with its no upset says the letters N and O inside the word are turned over to read the other way

parts.note: to snog is British slang for kissing passionately

explanation.surface: Serenading, and kissing without any upset to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOG is British slang for a passionate kiss; with its NO turned round it reads S-ON-GS. 'perhaps' marks serenades as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenades are one example of musical pieces sung, typically to a lover.

clue.text: Fib teen employed to get advantage

indicators.note: the letters are employed, put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A teenager tells a fib to gain an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage that something brings.

clue.text: Pirate cure can be fake

indicators.note: fake as a verb means to fabricate, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cure in a can might be bogus.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a sea robber of the Caribbean, a synonym for a pirate.

clue.text: Ranked as a lower-order batsman, direction is to keep in — or out

indicators.note: the direction is to keep, or hold inside it, the word in

parts.note: NTH is an abbreviation for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction about a tail-end batsman staying at the crease or getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: '— or out' is surface flourish: a batsman is either in or out. In cricket the batting order runs from 1 to 11, so number 9 is a lower-order, tail-end batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Batting at number nine of eleven places a cricketer in the lower order of the batting line-up.

clue.text: Officer needing loo in speech in US, that would be left here

definitions.text: Officer needing loo in speech in US, that would be left here

parts.words: Officer needing loo in speech in US, that would be left here
parts.note: Americans pronounce the rank 'loo-tenant', while the British say 'left-tenant'; so the first part of the British pronunciation is left, and in US speech the loo comes first

explanation.surface: An officer is desperate for the toilet while speaking in America.
explanation.walkthrough: British English says 'lef-tenant' and American English 'loo-tenant'; the clue plays on the loo coming first in the US version, and 'left' being heard in the British one.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior commissioned officer rank in the army or navy, the senior of the two lieutenant grades.

clue.text: Tricky criminal gets to carry can

indicators.note: the rearranged letters carry, or hold within them, the container
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted round

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A cunning crook manages to carry a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun for the crook, but it is the signal to rearrange, and 'to carry' puts the can inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A testing problem or time is one that is tricky and demanding.

clue.text: Malls that could possibly offer double parking?

definitions.text: Malls that could possibly offer double parking?

parts.words: Malls that could possibly offer double parking?
parts.note: retail complexes come with large car parks, so a shopper could park twice over; the clue plays on the idea of doubled parking

explanation.surface: A question about whether shopping complexes allow double parking.
explanation.walkthrough: Malls are the straight definition; the rest is a playful aside about their huge car parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Malls are large indoor complexes of stores, the American word for retail precincts.

clue.text: Someone pillaging downs a horseman

indicators.note: downs means drops or puts down, so the letter a is dropped from the word

parts.note: a raider is someone who pillages

explanation.surface: A looter overpowers a man on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downs' seems to mean knocks down; here it means drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a person on horseback, such as a jockey or cavalryman.

clue.text: Italians take this long to eat

definitions.text: Italians take this long to eat

parts.words: Italians take this long to eat
parts.note: the surface suggests slow eaters, but the long thing that Italians eat is a long thin pasta

explanation.surface: A remark that Italians are slow eaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this long' reads as a length of time; it is the long strands of a pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known long, thin strand pasta, a staple of Italian cooking.

clue.text: Facial adornment with ring in has to hurt

indicators.note: in puts the ring inside the word for obligation

parts.note: has to means must
a ring is shaped like the letter O
to hurt is to ache

explanation.surface: A facial piercing with a ring in it is bound to be painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a piercing, but it gives only the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a decoration of the face.

clue.text: PC at first, young conservative goes into ownership

indicators.note: at first puts the police officer at the start

parts.note: a PC (police constable) is a cop
the right is the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: A policeman starts out, then a young Tory gets into ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: PC here is police constable, not personal computer or political correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal ownership of a creative work and the right to reproduce it.

clue.text: Wishy-washy golf article

parts.note: something wishy-washy is weak or thin
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A feeble piece of golf writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece, or a grammatical 'the'; it means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: An article in the sense of an item or object is simply a thing.

clue.text: Prepared ten quiches — last lacking style

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
the word quiches is lacking its last letter

explanation.surface: A cook made ten quiches, but the final one was lacking in flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last lacking' drops the final S of 'quiches' to leave QUICHE, which joins TEN and 'Prepared' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Technique is a manner or method of performing, closely akin to someone's style.

clue.text: Cook that gets smashed in break

indicators.note: the word break is smashed in, broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A chef who gets drunk on a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' reads as drunk; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is a person whose job is to cook bread and cakes.

clue.text: Heading north from depots, substitute coaches pick up here?

indicators.note: Heading north says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions for a substitute vehicle heading north from the depots.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'from' as a link word; it is the signal that the letters are taken from inside 'depots, substitute'. In a down entry 'Heading north' reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside halt where buses, and by extension coaches, collect passengers.

clue.text: Light fixture that helps passengers leaving the plane

definitions.text: Light fixture that helps passengers leaving the plane

parts.words: Light fixture that helps passengers leaving the plane
parts.note: a light, fabric device fixed to a person that slows a jump from an aircraft; 'light fixture' pretends to be a lamp fitting

explanation.surface: A lighting fitting aboard an aircraft that guides disembarking passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light fixture' reads as a lamp; it is a lightweight thing strapped on to someone jumping out.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy device worn by someone jumping from an aircraft to slow the descent.

clue.text: Nearest broadcast is from China?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether the closest radio broadcast comes from China.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows China is one example of the region meant.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the Orient, so something from there is Oriental.

clue.text: Obstructed southern hideout used by European communist

parts.note: a nook is a secluded hiding place
a communist is called a Red

explanation.surface: A southern hideaway used by a European communist was blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a player is snookered when another ball blocks the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stymied or blocked, from the cue-sport position where no direct shot is open.

clue.text: All right to be got up in the style of Australian native

indicators.note: got up means raised, so in a down entry the letters are read upward

parts.note: OK means all right
à la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: Fine to dress up like an Australian native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' suggests dressed in costume; in a down clue it reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-dwelling marsupial found only in Australia, so it is native to that country.

clue.text: Runs local activity

definitions.meaning: dashes or moves quickly and suddenly
a pub game; in Britain the local is the neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: A pairing of running and a neighbourhood pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British slang for one's nearest pub, where the arrow-throwing game is traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to run swiftly; throwing arrows at a board is the classic British pub game.

clue.text: Requires niece's dish to be scrubbed evenly

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters are scrubbed out, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: A niece needs her dish scrubbed thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' looks like a cleaning instruction; it means the even letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it.

clue.text: Capital place where an old serviceman is always looked up to

definitions.text: Capital place where an old serviceman is always looked up to

parts.words: Capital place where an old serviceman is always looked up to
parts.note: the London square where Admiral Nelson stands atop a tall column, so people literally look up at him

explanation.surface: A capital location where a veteran is respected forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looked up to' means admired, and literally gazed upward: Nelson's statue tops his column in this London square.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous square in London, the capital, named after Nelson's naval victory and home to his column.

clue.text: Spooner's fish gone — work on the net!

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the first consonants of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: a cod is a fish
gone means past

explanation.surface: The fish has gone, so the work goes into the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' suggests a fishing net; it means the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A downloadable audio series is a piece of creative work published on the internet.

clue.text: Add cubes, maybe derived from small, insignificant number

parts.note: wee means tiny or insignificant
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Adding cubes, perhaps derived from a tiny unimportant number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cubes' suggests powers of a number; they are sugar cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping sugar cubes into a drink is one way to make it taste sweeter.
